_comment: The atom-type enum. Seeded from two sources only: the family contents listed in the concept spec sec. 4.1, and the keyword-action / keyword-ability titles parsed from CR 701 and 702 into the database. No entry is authored from recalled Magic knowledge; every one carries its source in `evidence`. Generated by src/cli/generate-atom-schema.ts - do not hand-edit this file; change the generator and rerun `npm run generate:atom-schema` instead. PRECEDENCE NOTE for an implementer matching atoms against this enum (Task 2 fix pass 2, Minor finding 2): PRODUCES::TOKENS and PRODUCES::CARDS_TO_GRAVEYARD overlap in shape with several cr_701 keyword-action entries (CREATE, POPULATE, AMASS, INCUBATE, INVESTIGATE all produce tokens; MILL, SURVEIL, MANIFEST_DREAD all put cards into a graveyard) - the generic PRODUCES type only matches a card whose text does NOT use one of those specific named keywords; a card using the keyword matches the keyword-action entry instead. From schema v15 (spec sec. 20, item V9) CREATE and MILL carry the same params as their generic twins TOKENS and CARDS_TO_GRAVEYARD, amount included, and submit validation drops a generic twin whose span overlaps the keyword atom on the same face: one fact, one atom, the keyword type kept.

object.description: The object that the action is done to. self: the object this text is on ("this ...", or its own name). other: the clause leaves out that object ("another"). any: any object that matches the clause.

actor.description: The player who sacrifices ("each opponent sacrifices": opponent; "sacrifice ...": you; "each player": any).

cost_type.description: free: the cost or the clause that has the sacrifice asks for nothing else ("Sacrifice a creature: ...", "Kicker—Sacrifice an artifact.", "you may sacrifice a creature", "Each opponent sacrifices a creature."). costed: it also asks for mana, the tap symbol or another payment ("{1}, Sacrifice a creature: ...", "{T}, Sacrifice a Treasure: ...", "you may pay {2} and sacrifice a creature"). The mana cost of the spell itself does not count.

decision.description: cost: the sacrifice pays for an ability or a spell. It is in an activation cost (the text before the colon, CR 602.1a), in a keyword cost ("Kicker—Sacrifice ...", "Equip—Sacrifice ...") or in an additional cost ("As an additional cost to cast this spell, sacrifice ..."). choice: the player may do it or not ("you may sacrifice ...", a clause with "unless", "discard a card or sacrifice a permanent"). forced: the text makes the player do it ("Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step.", "Each opponent sacrifices a creature.").
